Computer Science Overview

From the catalog

Computer Science Foundations

From the catalog

All students can take a self-assessment to attempt to place out of CS 2000 and CS 2001. Students who place out of CS 2000 and CS 2001 will instead substitute 4-5 semester hours of CS, CY, or DS coursework at the 3000 level or higher not otherwise required in the degree.

  • All of:
    • CS 1800 — Discrete Structures
    • CS 1802 — Seminar for CS 1800
  • All of:
    • CS 2000 — Introduction to Program Design and Implementation
    • CS 2001 — Lab for CS 2000
  • All of:
    • CS 2100 — Program Design and Implementation 1
    • CS 2101 — Lab for CS 2100

Computer Science Required Courses

  • CS 2484 — Principles of Human-Computer Interaction
  • CS 3000 — Algorithms and Data
  • All of:
    • CS 3100 — Program Design and Implementation 2
    • CS 3101 — Lab for CS 3100
  • One of:
    • CS 3200 — Introduction to Databases
    • CS 4100 — Artificial Intelligence
  • One of:

Khoury Approved Electives

From the catalog

With advisor approval, directed study, research, project study, and appropriate graduate-level courses may also be taken as upper-division electives.

Complete 4 semester hours from within the following options:

CS 2500 or higher, except CS 5010

CY 2000 or higher, except CY 4930

DS 2500 or higher, except DS 4900

  • Choose 4 semester hours from:
    • Any CS course numbered 2500–9999 (except CS 5010)
    • Any CY course numbered 2000–9999 (except CY 4930)
    • Any DS course numbered 2500–9999 (except DS 4900)
    • MKTG 4606 — Digital, Analytics, Technology, and Automation Research Practicum
